title: Andy Razaf and 'Louisiana' played
summary: Johnston notes Razaf is gravely ill; they play McPartland's arrangement of 'Louisiana'.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: But they really had to keep up the illusion there. I was looking at this album of yours called 'Shades of Bix'. And I notice that you have 'Louisiana' on here by J. Johnson and Andy Razaf M. Do you know that Andy Razaf
is here in the hospital and very near death right now?
Let's play his number for him shall we?
I like that. This is my arrangement of 'Louisiana'.
Well that was really 'Louisiana' wasn't it? (LAUGHTER). So that was out of Louisiana even if it wasn't out of New Orleans. (LAUGHTER). That's Chicago jazz, huh? (LAUGHTER). Because it swings.

It really swings, yes. And as Andy Razaf I mentioned just before we played it, was one of the three composers and that he is extremely ill and reported near death now here in a hospital in New York. And I think there's a thing to say here that he's lived in California as you know in a wheelchair practically for many, many years. But he wanted to spend his last days in New York. And he literally
refused to go back to California. And he said, this is where he belonged. And it does seems now that this is where he will live out his last days.
He was a great man and he will leave some beautiful music.

Oh yes, and again Eubie Blake said that he has never seen a lyricist who worked the way Andy did. He said he's never seen Andy create a word. A single word. You give him a tune and he's got it and its off and he really enjoyed working with him. Loved working with him. And of course he was a prolific writer.

And I first knew about him when I was just a little girl because he was in the first book of negro poets that I ever owned which was called 'Negro Poets and Their Poetry'. And when I talked to his wife there very recently, she's about his fourth wife, I think now, Alicia, when I talked to her recently she didn't know about this book of poems. You know, and so I read a couple of the poems to her. It's not his book, it's an anthology. But I read the poems to her over the telephone and she was quite amazed.
